title: Borderline Personality Disorder - BSV and Vocal Patterns
content:
DOCUMENT TYPE: BSV / Vocal

BSV / VOCAL SIGNALS: High Arousal during interpersonal stress or abandonment fears (rapid speech, raised voice, emotional lability). Low Valence (emptiness, self-loathing, anger). Rapid shifts in Dominance (from submissive to explosive). Voice often shows sudden pitch breaks, strain, or breathy quality during affective storms. Chronic emptiness may appear as flat, low-energy prosody between crises.

PATIENT-LANGUAGE EXAMPLES: "I feel empty inside all the time", "One minute I'm fine, the next I'm raging", "I can't stand being alone".

COUNTER-SIGNALS / NEGATIONS: Stable mood and consistent prosody across contexts, absence of abandonment terror or self-harm history argues against BPD.

PROVENANCE: Clinical observation and studies of emotional dysregulation in BPD.
